rootCause.summary: Web-only production renderer bug in the fork's chat font-scale wrapper. react-native-unistyles resolves styles to opaque CSS-class markers on web ({ unistyles_<hash>: {} }), so RNStyleSheet.flatten(baseStyle).fontSize is undefined. AnimatedMarkdownText coerced that to 0 via `?? 0`, and useChatScaleAnimatedTextStyle then unconditionally emitted fontSize = 0 * scale = 0. Because the animated style is applied last in the style array, it overrode the correct 16px base with a text-hiding font-size: 0px.

evidenceDomBeforeFix.generatedCssClass: .unistyles_fzz3g0uonw { font-family: IBMPlexSans-Regular; font-size: 0px; line-height: 24px; margin-top: 8px; margin-bottom: 8px; color: var(--colors-text); font-weight: 400; }

flattenProbe.conclusion: Neither react-native nor react-native-unistyles flatten surfaces numeric fontSize/lineHeight on web; the values live only in the emitted CSS class.

rootCause.nativeContrast: On native, flatten resolves the real numeric fontSize (16), so scaling works and the bug never manifested — hence web-only and latent (the e-ink tablet target is native).

fix.change: useChatScaleAnimatedTextStyle now only emits `fontSize` when the resolved base is a positive number. This extends the existing `typeof style.fontSize === 'number'` guard in scaleMonoFonts with an added `> 0` clause, needed because `?? 0` callers inject a literal 0 that a bare typeof check would wrongly treat as a valid size. AnimatedMarkdownText passes the possibly-undefined flattened fontSize through instead of coercing to 0. When the base cannot be resolved (web/unistyles), no fontSize override is emitted and the base unistyles class's font-size survives. On native, the base resolves to a real number, so the animated scale applies exactly as before.
fix.einkSafety: Native path is byte-for-byte unchanged (base fontSize is a real number > 0, so fontSize is emitted and scaled identically). No animation, smooth-streaming, or normal production behavior added or altered.
